topics.label: Course overview and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the aims, structure, and learning outcomes of the lecture on the causes of cancer.

topics.label: Concepts and evidence for multifactorial cancer etiology
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the fundamental causes of cancer by balancing intrinsic cellular processes, genetic predisposition, and environmental factors supported by epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how biological agents, including viruses, bacteria, and parasites, contribute to cancer development, illustrated by Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Aflatoxin activation and dietary carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: It details how dietary aflatoxin is metabolically converted into a reactive epoxide that forms DNA adducts.

topics.label: UV radiation and DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: It explains how UV radiation acts as a physical carcinogen by inducing thymine dimers in DNA.

topics.label: Chemical carcinogens and xenobiotic metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: They examine chemical carcinogens that undergo metabolic processing or generate oxidative stress to cause DNA damage and tissue-specific mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion and non-mutagenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis where chronic inflammation and promoter signalling stimulate clonal expansion.

topics.label: Developmental timing and tissue susceptibility to carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: It explains how active cell proliferation during specific developmental stages alters tissue susceptibility to mutagens.

topics.label: Mutational signatures from genomic sequencing
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the identification of carcinogen-specific DNA damage patterns through whole-genome sequencing.

topics.label: Epidemiological cohort studies and biobanks
topics.groupedBecause: It explains how human epidemiological biobanks and biomarker tracking are used to associate environmental exposures with cancer.

topics.label: In vivo rodent bioassays and dosing challenges
topics.groupedBecause: It evaluates the methodology and limitations of using whole-animal rodent bioassays to assess carcinogen toxicity.

topics.label: The Ames test and in vitro mutagenesis screening
topics.groupedBecause: It details the bacterial Ames assay for detecting chemical mutagenicity and discusses the limitations of in vitro testing.

topics.label: Risk-benefit analysis and lecture summary
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental carcinogenesis and the personal assessment of exposure risks versus benefits.
